anomaly_def.Name: Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : Sustained physical read- and write-volume overruns the bandwidth or latency capability of the underlying storage devices.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Critical database volumes run out of free space, preventing further allocation to data, log, temp, or backup files.
Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly : Kernel-enforced ceilings on file handles, shared memory, threads, or AIO contexts are reached by database processes.

When all three root causes strike simultaneously, the database experiences a compound failure mode: rising I/O queue depths and latency slow every read and write, just as space-allocation operations and background writers begin to fail, while the engine is intermittently denied new file handles, shared-memory segments, or AIO slots needed to continue processing. Observable symptoms co-exist and amplify one another—high I/O wait time alongside space-exhaustion or auto-extend errors, cascading log-archive stalls, sudden "too many open files" or "cannot allocate shared memory" errors, checkpoints that cannot complete, and sessions hanging in both I/O and kernel wait states. Batch windows stretch, OLTP requests time out, and portions of the engine may appear up yet accept no new work.

Causally, storage-bandwidth saturation elongates every write, delaying checkpointing, archiving, and space-reclaim tasks, which accelerates space consumption. As free space dwindles, emergency auto-extension, log-switch, and purge operations raise the number of concurrent file opens and asynchronous I/O requests, pushing the process toward kernel limits. Once OS resource ceilings are hit, the engine is unable to create new files or I/O contexts, further throttling throughput and blocking the very maintenance needed to relieve space pressure. In parallel, failure to create or extend files feeds back into higher I/O retry traffic and excessive log buildup, worsening both throughput saturation and space exhaustion. The intertwined feedback loops of bandwidth starvation, capacity depletion, and kernel denials drive the database into a progressively deeper stall or partial outage until at least one of the constraints is lifted.

entry.official_description: At least one partial revoke exists on a database. The system variable '@@partial_revokes' must be set to ON.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
